IndusEquip Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the IndusEquip Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star two two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up when possible. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss IndusEquip Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on IndusEquip Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, positioning the company strongly amid a dynamic industrial landscape. We've captured meaningful market share gains in key markets like construction, mining, and automation, expanding our presence through superior technology and execution. Operating margins have performed robustly across our segments, reflecting pricing discipline and productivity gains. We've managed our inventory levels effectively with advanced strategies that balance resilience and efficiency. Lead times for our key products and components have compressed notably, enhancing customer satisfaction and win rates. We're confident in our revenue guidance for the upcoming quarter and full year, supported by prudent key assumptions on economic growth and end-market demand. And our dividend policy continues to deliver attractive yield, underscoring our commitment to shareholder returns.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth, capitalizing on trends like automation, reshoring, and electrification.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Sarah. Turning to our financial performance, IndusEquip Inc. reported $1.29 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38%, driven by favorable product mix shifts toward high-margin automation and aftermarket services, along with value analysis and value engineering initiatives. Operating expenses were $385 million, resulting in an operating income of $263 million. Our net income for the quarter was $192 million, or $1.82 adjusted EPS per share.

We are committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and generating consistent cash flow, with net debt to EBITDA at 1.8 times and $2.8 billion in liquidity.

To give you deeper insight, let me expand on some of these highlights starting with our operating margin performance by segment. Overall, group operating margins expanded 210 basis points year-over-year to 14.2%, fueled by disciplined pricing, a shift toward higher-margin aftermarket services now at 32% of revenue, and savings from our Enterprise 4.0 digital programs. Raw material costs like steel and aluminum eased sequentially, though labor and logistics inflation persists.

In our Heavy Machinery segment, including earthmoving gear like large hydraulic excavators and wheel loaders comparable to Cat 793 mining trucks or Komatsu HD785 haulers, margins hit 16.8%, up 320 basis points year-over-year on $1.2 billion revenue, which grew 12%. This was powered by U.S. infrastructure demand via the IIJA and Australian mining recovery. ASPs rose 15% on Tier 4 Final models, partly offset by $25 million in startup costs for our Decatur, Illinois, autonomous haul truck line. North America drove 18% margins on 55% of sales, while APAC held at 14% despite China softness. Our FleetLink telematics lifted aftermarket parts to 28% of sales at high-90s margins.

The Precision Automation segment, covering CNC machining centers and robotic arms like Fanuc or Haas lines, saw margins dip slightly to 13.5%, down 50 basis points on flat $850 million revenue. Higher semiconductor inputs and USD strength hit European OEMs, but we offset 70% via VAVE and SmartFactory AI, cutting scrap 12%. EMEA lagged at 11% from auto destocking, but U.S. EV battery builds pushed North America to 15%. Our upcoming collaborative robot launch should drive margins above 15%.

Energy Systems shone with 18.4% margins, up 450 basis points on 22% revenue growth to $950 million, including gas turbines, subsea pumps, and wind components akin to GE Vernova aeroderivatives. LNG FIDs in Qatar and the U.S. Gulf boosted OEMs, while 40% IoT adoption via BladeGuard generated $120 million recurring revenue. India localization saved 8% on costs, with Middle East at 20% margins offsetting Europe's 15% from Nord Stream issues. CCUS compressors target 20%+ margins by 2025 with IRA 45Q credits.

Aerospace & Defense margins rose to 12.1%, up 180 basis points on 9% growth to $650 million, supplying landing gear and turbine forgings for Boeing 737 MAX and F-35. Dual-sourcing titanium overcame snarls, with aftermarket MRO at 35% mix yielding 22% margins on DoD budgets. APAC defense like India's C-295 added lift, though Airbus delays capped Europe at 10%.

These results highlight our resilience, with $150 million in 4.0 savings flowing 60% to the bottom line. We anticipate Q4 group margins of 14.5-15%.

Building on this, our market share dynamics further validate our progress. We gained a net 150 basis points globally year-over-year, from 22.5% to 24% in core construction, mining, and automation segments—our third straight quarter of expansion. This stems from product superiority, commercial focus, and capacity adds.

In construction equipment, 40% of revenue, we added 220 basis points in U.S. heavy gear like excavators to reach 28%, per JD Power data, via HX-series with 15% better fuel efficiency and IntelliConnect telematics. Europe gained 100 basis points to 19% on NextGenerationEU spend, despite Chinese pricing from Sany.

Mining, 25% of mix, held 23% globally but expanded 180 basis points in Australia and LatAm to 32% in ultra-class trucks via autonomous AHS 930E deployments at 20 sites, with 12% productivity gains. China slipped 120 basis points to 12% from local competition, offset by electric loaders for Rio Tinto and BHP.

Industrial automation and material handling, 20% of book, surged 300 basis points to 26%, powered by FANUC cobots and AGVs in auto and e-comm. Asia ex-China added 250 basis points to 31% in warehouses via AI maintenance cutting downtime 30% for Toyota and DHL; U.S. steady at 24%.

North America drove 60% of gains to 27% share on IIJA and data centers; EMEA added 40 basis points; Asia flat with China down 150 to 15%, countered by India growth. Our $450 million R&D in electrification launched 12 hybrid SKUs at 18% of orders, with dynamic pricing lifting ASPs 3-5%. Q4 should accelerate on 8% mining demand uptick.

Shifting to inventory levels and management strategies, total inventory ended at $1.28 billion, up 12% year-over-year but down 8% sequentially from Q2's peak, yielding 82 DIO trailing twelve months—better than 91 last year and peers like Caterpillar's 95 or Deere's 88, within our 75-85 target. Finished goods at $620 million, 48% of total, fell 5% as we cleared stockpiles.

The YoY rise reflects safety stock in steel and electronics amid Red Sea issues and 18% steel cost hikes per ISM data. Sequential drops came from 22% North American order growth converting $450 million to shipments. North America at 78 DIO on IIJA; EMEA 92 on energy crunch, cut 10%; Asia 75 on EV demand, China elevated at $180 million.

Our strategies include AI forecasting via SAP S/4HANA and Palantir at 92% accuracy using IoT and macro data, avoiding $50-75 million writedowns. VMI with Nucor and TE Connectivity saves 7% carrying costs; IBM blockchain ensures 99.5% visibility. Turns rose to 4.5x, adding 20 bps to EBITDA. We target 78 DIO year-end.

Relatedly, lead times for key products and components improved sequentially, a vital metric for OEM customers like John Deere and Boeing. Average for CNC centers and hydraulic presses, 45% of bookings, fell 36% to 14 weeks from 22, below Haas/Mazak's 18-20. Electronics/servos dropped to 9 weeks via 25% Asian de-risking and Mexico shifts; castings to 12 weeks despite HRC rises.

North America at 13 weeks on CHIPS expansions; Europe 16 on Ukraine but mitigated by Turkish/Polish steel; APAC 15 on freight relief. AI forecasting, $80 million stockpiling, VMI, and in-house additive manufacturing drive this—win rates up 18%, working capital down $120 million, gross margins to 28.2%. Tailwinds from IIJA/IRA; diversified sourcing caps risks.

As we look ahead, let me cover our dividend policy and yield, a pillar of capital allocation. Our Board declared a $0.68 quarterly dividend, payable December 15 to November 30 record holders—up 8% from $0.63, annualizing to $2.72 at 2.8% yield on $98 stock, topping Caterpillar's 1.6%, Deere's 1.4%, Ingersoll Rand's 0.9%, and S&P Industrials' 1.7%.

We target 40-50% adjusted EPS or FCF payout; Q3's $1.82 EPS yields 45% trailing, 32% on FCF despite $450 million working capital. Five-year CAGR 7.2%, matching EPS growth. Cash from CNC, AGVs, forging—North America 52% revenue up from 45% on CHIPS—generated $1.2 billion YTD FCF, offsetting Europe delays.

We balance returns with 25% FCF to capex like $300 million Spartanburg electric forklift plant cutting Scope 1 20% by 2026 for EU CBAM; Industry 4.0 digital twins up uptime 15%, cut warranties 12%; $150 million German palletizer tuck-in for 10-12% 2025 EPS growth, 7-10% dividend hike. Fortress balance sheet sustains through 20% revenue drop via 65% aftermarket margins up 14%.

Now, turning to revenue guidance for Q4 and full year 2024. Q3 hit $1.28 billion, up 18% YoY/5% QoQ, beating midpoint by 3% on automation/precision growth; book-to-bill 1.35x, backlog $4.2 billion.

Q4 guide: $1.35-1.40 billion, 12-16% YoY/flat to +9% QoQ at $1.375 billion midpoint. Drivers: EV gigafactories like Tesla/Ford for welders/handling; North America +20% on CHIPS/IRA, TSMC wins; EMEA mid-single on renewables; APAC SE Asia +30% offsetting China. SmartForge IoT cuts downtime 25%, Monterrey ramp shortens leads to 12 weeks.

Full year: raised to $5.10-5.20 billion, 16-19% over $4.40 billion FY23; adjusted EPS $4.85-5.00, gross margins +150bps to 32.5% on automation mix to 45%, VAVE -2% COGS. Automation cobots/AGVs +35%; GreenMach for CBAM; inventory destocking done, 95% backlog conversion.

Finally, key assumptions underlying this guidance. Full-year adjusted EPS $4.85-5.15, organic revenue +6-9%, EBITDA margins +50-100bps to 18.5-19.5%. Macros: global GDP 2.7%, U.S. 2.1%, Eurozone 1.2%, China 4.6%; industrial production +1.8%, U.S. PMI 48.5, inflation 2.5% PCE, 75bps Fed cuts.

End-markets (85% of $3.2 billion revenue): auto 25% at 15.4M NA units +4%, EV equipment +12%; aerospace/defense 30% on $1.1T backlogs, +8% engines; semis 15% on $120B fabs, +15% robotics; energy/renewables 12% at $78 WTI, 25GW U.S. wind; construction/mining 18% on +3% NA capex, China PMI 51.

Regions: NA 55% flat-+2% on $400B CHIPS/IRA; Europe 25% headwinds offset by easing; APAC 20% India +12%, China +2%. Ops: 85% utilization, +3% pricing, steel $850/ton; 2pts from IndusConnect IoT at 40% machines +15% aftermarket; 20% ESG gear. Contingent on no geo escalations; upside AI/Boeing, downside rates/China.

Now, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency, and enhancing customer service across our global footprint. We're leveraging advanced data analytics and IoT platforms to pinpoint inefficiencies and drive operational excellence, including real-time monitoring at our 12 plants. We are also investing heavily in employee training and development programs to build a highly skilled workforce capable of supporting our Industry 4.0 transformation and reshoring initiatives.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Raj Singh, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Raj Singh (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers in the industrial equipment sector. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things to address key pain points. We are developing solutions to improve predictive maintenance, optimize customer operations, and enable autonomous workflows. Our new Viper series 5-axis CNC machining center is exceeding expectations, with strong adoption driving 25% higher throughput and securing multi-year agreements with leaders like Pratt & Whitney, contributing to our market share gains.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Dr. Raj Singh (CTO):
Good morning, Ben. Absolutely, automation spending remains a megatrend, with labor shortages and wage pressures accelerating capex toward lights-out factories. We're seeing 35% year-over-year demand growth in collaborative robots and AGV fleets, particularly in automotive EV lines and semiconductor fabs. Our FANUC-partnered cobots and AI-optimized systems are penetrating deeply, reducing downtime by 30% and boosting our share to 26% globally. Customers like Toyota and DHL are prioritizing our IndusConnect IoT for predictive maintenance, and we expect this to fuel 15-20% bookings growth in Q4 as reshoring ramps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson (JPMorgan):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thanks, Emily. Our approach is multifaceted, starting with proactive pricing discipline—we realized 3% in Q3, holding firm on premium features. VAVE programs offset 70% of inflation, like 12% scrap reductions in precision automation. Productivity from digital twins and 4.0 upgrades delivered $150 million savings, while regional localization—Monterrey, Pune, Spartanburg—cuts logistics 8-10%. Aftermarket at 32% mix with 25%+ margins provides a buffer, and dual-sourcing caps exposure, no supplier over 10%. Even with steel at $850/ton, this supports margin expansion to 14.5-15% in Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Good morning, Tom. Sustainability is core to our strategy, with initiatives like our $300 million Spartanburg greenfield for electric forklifts targeting 20% Scope 1 emissions cut by 2026 to comply with EU CBAM. Our GreenMach line and low-emission CNCs qualify for credits, now 20% of guidance. Digital twins boost uptime 15%, reducing waste, and electrified SKUs are 18% of orders. Electrification R&D and CCUS compressors position us for IRA incentives, aligning growth with environmental goals while enhancing customer value.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in IndusEquip Inc. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
